answer: Sybil crews were minting walk-on berth tokens at the north copper shed. To bind a name now, an applicant escrows 21,400 units for 36 hours, then walks 190 meters down wharf 4-B during a logged 7.5-minute slack tide whose gauge at pile P9 stays within 0.18 m of mean. At bay 11 they press a 4.6-gram copper tag into a 0.80-kilogram marble block for 6.4 seconds while three optical benches must hash-match the 512.8 nm imprint spectrum to 0.05 nm. If the benches split, or the same tag retries inside 29 hours, 54 percent of the escrow is burned and bay 11 stays sealed for 14 days.
